turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that they would find another way to care for their son, that O-lan's health was the most important thing

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she had been thinking, and there was no other way to provide for their son's future than to arrange his marriage to the woman they had chosen, so that he would be well taken care of.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan's concerns for their son's future were misplaced, that he was strong and capable of providing for himself, and that their son's happiness was more important than any material security.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung with a mixture of sadness and determination in her eyes, and told him that he did not understand the importance of securing their son's future, that a stable family was the only thing that brought her peace.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son assured his mother that he would work hard to ensure his future and make her proud, and looked to his father for guidance and support

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he had spoken to the matchmaker and that a suitable bride had already been found, and that she would be pleased with the selection.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son if he knew of the bride's family and their circumstances, her eyes fixed intently on her son's face

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son told his mother that the bride's family, the Lin family, were known to be a respectable and hardworking clan, and their daughter was said to be a kind and gentle soul.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son to be certain that the marriage arrangements were made with the utmost care, and that the bride's family was treated with the respect they deserved.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid asked O-lan if there was anything else she needed to attend to, her voice barely above a whisper as she glanced nervously at the eldest son.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she must not worry about the arrangements for their son's marriage, that he would take care of it, and that she should rest now.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung to promise her that the marriage arrangements would be made before she passed away

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he would see to it that the marriage arrangements were made as soon as possible, and that he would choose a good match for himself.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan urged Wang Lung that the time was running out, and the marriage must be arranged soon, for the eldest son's sake, as well as their own.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung urged O-lan to be patient and not to worry about the future, for he would provide for their son and give him a good life, no matter what happened.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was not concerned about the future, but about ensuring the eldest son's marriage and prosperity, for she knew that Wang Lung's efforts would not be enough to provide for their son's well-being in the long run.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son assured his mother that he would find a good wife and establish a prosperous household, just as she wanted, and that he would make her proud.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her son that she was glad he had made his promise, but that she still worried about his future and the future of their family.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son told O-lan that she must not worry, that he was strong and would take care of the family

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was glad the eldest son had spoken to her, but she still worried about the future and the family's well-being.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
